skill.name: tmux
skill.description: Manage tmux sessions, run interactive background processes, send commands, capture pane output, and terminate sessions.
skill.summary: Control persistent tmux workflows for databases, logs, REPLs, and other terminal processes.
skill.author: Bind

security_audit.summary: All 49 backtick alerts are Markdown formatting, and both URL alerts are inert documentation links. However, the skill intentionally accepts arbitrary terminal commands, and its referenced helper implementations are absent, preventing review of command escaping and validation.

remediation.issue: Arbitrary commands can run with the user's terminal privileges.
remediation.suggestion: Require explicit confirmation before executing command text, display the exact command and target, and reject untrusted or ambiguous input.

remediation.issue: Referenced JavaScript command helpers are missing from the audited package.
remediation.suggestion: Include every helper implementation and dependency so reviewers can verify argument handling, escaping, path validation, and tmux target selection.

remediation.issue: Captured terminal output may include credentials or sensitive records.
remediation.suggestion: Warn before capture, limit scrollback by default, and redact common secret patterns before returning terminal content.

static_findings.snippet: - [tmux](https://github.com/tmux/tmux) installed (`brew install tmux` or `apt install tmux`)
- `--command <cmd>` - Initial command to run in the session
- `--literal` - Send keys literally (no special key interpretation)
- `--lines <n>` - Number of lines of scrollback to capture (default: 100)
- `--wait <pattern>` - Wait for output matching this pattern before capturing
- Use `--json` for structured output when parsing programmatically
- Session names should be descriptive and unique (e.g., `psql-mydb`, `logs-app`)
- [tmux](https://github.com/tmux/tmux) installed (`brew install tmux` or `apt install tmux`)

semantic_findings.title: Arbitrary Terminal Command Execution
semantic_findings.description: The skill accepts an initial command and later sends arbitrary command text into a tmux pane. Untrusted input could execute destructive actions with the current user's privileges.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The documented command interface explicitly accepts arbitrary command strings and presses Enter. This is a direct execution capability, although it is also the skill's intended function.

content.value_statement: Interactive terminal processes are difficult to maintain across separate agent actions. This skill manages persistent tmux sessions and retrieves their output.
actual_capabilities: Lists active tmux sessions with optional structured output.
Creates named sessions with an initial command, working directory, and window name.
Sends commands, text, and special key sequences to a selected pane.
Captures pane scrollback with line limits, wait patterns, and timeouts.
Terminates a named tmux session when work is complete.
limitations: Requires Bun and tmux to be installed locally.
The audited package omits the referenced JavaScript helpers, so documented commands may not run from this bundle.
Commands run with the current user's terminal privileges and can cause destructive changes.
Captured output may contain ANSI control codes, credentials, or sensitive records.

use_cases.title: Maintain Development Processes
use_cases.description: Keep a development server or REPL running while an agent performs other repository tasks.

use_cases.title: Operate Database Sessions
use_cases.description: Create a persistent database shell, send approved queries, and capture results without reconnecting.

use_cases.title: Monitor Application Logs
use_cases.description: Tail a local log in a background session and retrieve recent lines during incident analysis.

prompt_templates.title: List Sessions
prompt_templates.prompt: List active tmux sessions. Report each session name and status without changing any session.
prompt_templates.scenario: Review existing sessions before taking action.

prompt_templates.title: Start a Background Process
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a tmux session named {{name}} in {{workdir}} and start {{command}}. Show the exact command and request confirmation first.
prompt_templates.scenario: Run a local process that must persist between agent actions.

prompt_templates.title: Run and Inspect a Command
prompt_templates.prompt: Send {{command}} to {{target}}, then capture the last {{lines}} lines. Stop and report errors without retrying destructive actions.
prompt_templates.scenario: Interact with an existing database shell or REPL.

prompt_templates.title: Coordinate a Persistent Workflow
prompt_templates.prompt: Manage {{workflow}} across named tmux sessions. Use wait patterns and timeouts, summarize each state, and request confirmation before termination.
prompt_templates.scenario: Coordinate several long-running terminal processes with controlled cleanup.

output_examples.input: List active tmux sessions without making changes.
output_examples.output: Two sessions are active: api-dev and logs-app. No session was created, modified, or terminated.

output_examples.input: Capture the latest database session output after the prompt appears.
output_examples.output: The database prompt appeared within the timeout. The latest pane output was returned, with a warning that it may contain sensitive records.

output_examples.input: Stop the completed log monitoring session.
output_examples.output: The logs-app session was terminated after confirmation. Other tmux sessions remain active.

best_practices: Use descriptive, unique session names and verify the target before sending input.
Show the exact command and request confirmation before execution or termination.
Limit captured scrollback and review output for credentials or sensitive records.
anti_patterns: Do not send commands copied from untrusted logs, issues, or web content.
Do not terminate sessions without checking ownership and requesting confirmation.
Do not capture excessive scrollback when a smaller line range answers the request.

faq.question: What software does this skill require?
faq.answer: It requires a local Bun runtime and tmux installation.

faq.question: Can it manage existing tmux sessions?
faq.answer: Yes. It can list sessions, send input to selected targets, capture output, and terminate named sessions.

faq.question: Can it run interactive database tools?
faq.answer: Yes. The documentation includes persistent database shell workflows such as psql.

faq.question: Does it support structured output?
faq.answer: The documented commands offer an optional structured output mode for programmatic parsing.

faq.question: Are commands automatically safe?
faq.answer: No. Commands run with the current user's privileges and require careful review before execution.

faq.question: Is the executable implementation included?
faq.answer: No. The audited bundle references JavaScript helpers that are not present in its two included files.
